mainTopic: Missing הבדלה in a make-up prayer, and whether the daily prayers come from the אבות or match the קרבנות, with their time limits
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about someone who missed מנחה on ערב שבת or on שבת and makes it up by praying two עמידות at night. The ברייתא implies that if he left הבדלה out of the first עמידה on מוצאי שבת, it does not count. A תוספתא seems to say the opposite: forgetting הבדלה does not require going back, because it can be said over wine. The גמרא leaves this as a קשיא. Then a new topic begins: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the אבות instituted the prayers, while רבי יהושע בן לוי says they were set up to match the תמידין. Each side has a ברייתא. One ties שחרית, מנחה and ערבית to אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. The other ties each prayer's deadline to its קרבן, and it defines מנחה גדולה and מנחה קטנה. The גמרא clarifies that רבי יהודה's פלג המנחה is the midpoint of the later מנחה. It also explains that even רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא agrees the רבנן based the prayers on the קרבנות, as מוסף proves. Finally, the גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's 'until four hours' includes the fourth hour, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Making up a missed afternoon prayer around שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who missed מנחה on ערב שבת or on שבת prays two עמידות that night. On מוצאי שבת he says הבדלה only in the first. If he says it only in the second, the first does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone forgot to pray מנחה on Friday, he prays two עמידות on Friday night. If he forgot מנחה on שבת, he prays two weekday עמידות on מוצאי שבת. He says הבדלה in the first one but not in the second. If he said הבדלה in the second and not in the first, the second counts and the first does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with the rules for making up a missed מנחה when the next prayer falls on שבת night or on מוצאי שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The make-up rule is simple: pray the next prayer twice. On מוצאי שבת there is an extra detail. הבדלה belongs in the first עמידה, which is the night's real prayer, and not in the second, which makes up the missed מנחה. If he reversed it, only the second counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a mistake, he forgot
Friday, the day before שבת
Saturday night, after שבת ends
Says הבדלה, which separates שבת from the weekday
It counted for him, he fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two night prayers are interchangeable. The first is the night's own prayer and the second is the make-up, which is why הבדלה goes only in the first.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל מִנְחָה בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: If someone made a mistake and did not pray the afternoon prayer on Friday,
he prays two on Friday night.
phrases.notes: Two עמידות: one for the night itself and one to make up the missed מנחה.

phrases.english: If he made a mistake and did not pray the afternoon prayer on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁל חוֹל.
phrases.english: he prays two weekday prayers on Saturday night.
He says havdala in the first one,
phrases.notes: This is the הבדלה said inside the עמידה, in the ברכה of חונן הדעת.

phrases.english: and he does not say havdala in the second.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הִבְדִּיל בַּשְּׁנִיָּה וְלֹא הִבְדִּיל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
phrases.english: And if he said havdala in the second and not in the first,
the second one counts for him,
the first one does not count for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with a ברייתא on making up missed prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed מנחה is made up by praying two עמידות at the next prayer. On מוצאי שבת, הבדלה goes in the first. If it was said only in the second, the first does not count.

steps.title: Does forgetting הבדלה make a prayer not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא: a prayer without הבדלה is treated as if he never prayed, so he must repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that because he did not say הבדלה in the first עמידה, it is as if he did not pray, and we make him go back and pray again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls a general rule out of the ברייתא's last line. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the first prayer 'did not count' when הבדלה was missing from it. That seems to mean any עמידה without הבדלה on מוצאי שבת is invalid and must be repeated. The question is phrased as a question, but it states the inference so the גמרא can test it against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Used to draw out what a source implies
The first one
He is like someone who did not pray
We make him go back and repeat

phrases.english: Is that to say that since
he did not say havdala in the first one,
he is considered like someone who did not pray,
and we make him go back and pray again?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the ברייתא's last line.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether leaving out הבדלה invalidates the עמידה so that he must repeat it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct answer is given. The inference is challenged in the next step.

steps.title: A source says you do not repeat for missing הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: A תוספתא says that someone who forgets the rain mentions goes back, but someone who forgets הבדלה in חונן הדעת does not, because he can say it over wine. This contradicts the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: If someone forgot to mention the power of rain in תחיית המתים, or the request for rain in ברכת השנים, we make him go back. But if he forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not make him go back, because he can say it over the cup of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 2 by quoting a source that says forgetting הבדלה does not require repeating the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 implied that a prayer without הבדלה does not count. The תוספתא says the opposite: forgetting הבדלה is not a reason to go back, because he can still say it over wine. Missing rain mentions is different, since they can only be said in the prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction
Mentioning God's power of rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם)
The request for rain (ותן טל ומטר)
The ninth ברכה, asking for a good year
The fourth ברכה, where הבדלה is added on מוצאי שבת
Over a cup of wine

phrases.english: And they pointed out a contradiction:
If he made a mistake and did not mention the power of rain
in the blessing about reviving the dead,
or the request for rain in the blessing of the years,
we make him go back.
But if he forgot havdala in "Who grants knowledge,"
we do not make him go back,
because he can say it over the cup!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the ברייתא that a prayer without הבדלה does not count and must be repeated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא rules that forgetting הבדלה in the עמידה does not require going back, because it can be said over wine. That directly contradicts the idea that the prayer is invalid.

steps.title: The contradiction is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'קשיא': the contradiction between the ברייתא and the תוספתא stays as a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer here and leaves the contradiction open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for why the ברייתא treats a prayer without הבדלה as not counting while the תוספתא says not to go back. The word קשיא marks a real difficulty that stays unanswered. It does not mean either source is thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The problem stays unanswered
A full refutation. This stronger word is not used here

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא is not the same as תיובתא. Here neither source is rejected; the גמרא just leaves the question open.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא implies a prayer without הבדלה does not count. The תוספתא says you do not go back for missing הבדלה because you can say it over wine. The גמרא leaves this as a קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 3 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction about whether forgetting הבדלה requires repeating the עמידה stays unresolved.

steps.title: The אבות instituted the prayers
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the daily prayers were instituted by the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The prayers were instituted by the אבות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about where the three daily prayers came from, beginning with the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, praying three times a day goes back to אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. This opinion will be contrasted with רבי יהושע בן לוי's view in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. Introduces a dispute between אמוראים
The Patriarchs: אברהם, יצחק, יעקב
They instituted them

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the background for the משנה's argument about how late each prayer may be said, which the גמרא will connect to the תמידין.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
The prayers were instituted by the Patriarchs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the הבדלה question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daily prayers were instituted by the אבות.

steps.title: The prayers were set up to match the daily offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees and says the prayers were instituted to match the תמידין, the daily קרבנות in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The prayers were instituted to correspond to the תמידין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the dispute: the prayers are modeled on the daily קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gave the prayers an older source in the אבות. רבי יהושע בן לוי instead ties them to the תמידין in the בית המקדש. On his view the prayers take the place of the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Corresponding to, matching
The daily קרבנות brought in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the source of the prayers: the אבות (רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא) or the תמידין (רבי יהושע בן לוי).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The prayers were instituted to correspond to the daily offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prayers were instituted to correspond to the תמידין.

steps.title: Both opinions have a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא and another ברייתא supporting רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא that agrees with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, and there is a ברייתא that agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next steps. It tells us that each of the two opinions we just heard has a ברייתא backing it up, and it will now show each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side of the מחלוקת now has support from a ברייתא, which is an older teaching from the time of the תנאים. That means neither opinion gets pushed aside. Both stay strong.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
In agreement with him
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: and it was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Announces support for both opinions given in steps 5 and 6.
steps.raayaObject: Both the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא and the opinion of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two separate ברייתות, which are brought in the next steps.

steps.title: אברהם set up שחרית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא begins: אברהם set up שחרית. We learn this because the פסוק says he 'stood' in the morning, and 'standing' means תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that agrees with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says: אברהם set up the morning תפילה. The פסוק says that אברהם got up early in the morning to the place where he had 'stood.' 'Standing' always means תפילה, as we see from the פסוק that says פינחס 'stood and prayed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the first ברייתא. It shows from a פסוק that אברהם davened in the morning, so he set up שחרית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works in two steps. First, a פסוק says אברהם went in the morning to where he had 'stood.' Second, a different פסוק uses 'stood' together with 'prayed' when talking about פינחס. Putting them together, אברהם's 'standing' in the morning was תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up, instituted
The morning תפילה
Standing; here it means תפילה
'X means nothing other than Y': a way of defining a word in a פסוק

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: It was taught in agreement with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא:
Avraham set up the morning prayer,
as it says: "And Avraham rose early in the morning
to the place where he had stood",
and 'standing' means nothing other than prayer,
as it says: "And Pinchas stood and prayed."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אַבְרָהָם תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing the first ברייתא that step 7 announced.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view that the תפילות were set up by the אבות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 19:27, read together with תהלים 106:30 ('standing' means prayer).

steps.title: יצחק set up מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: יצחק set up מנחה. We learn this because he went out to 'converse' in the field toward evening, and 'conversation' means תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יצחק set up the afternoon תפילה. The פסוק says that יצחק went out to 'converse' in the field toward evening. 'Conversation' always means תפילה, as we see from the פסוק that says a poor person pours out his 'conversation' before ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues with the second אב. It shows that יצחק davened as evening was coming, so he set up מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof works the same way as the one for אברהם. The time of day comes from the first פסוק: 'toward evening,' which is מנחה time. The second פסוק shows that the word שיחה means תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon תפילה
Conversation, talking; here it means תפילה
Toward evening

phrases.english: Yitzchak set up the afternoon prayer,
as it says: "And Yitzchak went out to converse in the field
toward evening",
and 'conversation' means nothing other than prayer,
as it says: "A prayer of the poor person when he is faint
and pours out his conversation before ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the second אב.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view that the תפילות were set up by the אבות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 24:63, read together with תהלים 102:1 ('conversation' means prayer).

steps.title: יעקב set up ערבית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: יעקב set up ערבית. We learn this because he 'encountered' the place where he slept at night, and 'encountering' means תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב set up the evening תפילה. The פסוק says he 'encountered' the place and slept there. 'Encountering' always means תפילה, as we see from what ה׳ told ירמיהו: do not pray for this people, and do not 'encounter' Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the third אב. It shows that יעקב davened at night, so he set up ערבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about ירמיהו puts 'do not pray' right next to 'do not encounter Me.' That shows the word פגיעה can mean תפילה. Since יעקב 'encountered' the place where he spent the night, he davened at night. With this, all three תפילות have been tied to the three אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: The evening תפילה
Encountering, reaching out; here it means תפילה
And he spent the night

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא: אברהם set up שחרית ('standing'), יצחק set up מנחה ('conversation'), and יעקב set up ערבית ('encountering').

phrases.english: Yaakov set up the evening prayer,
as it says: "And he encountered the place and spent the night there",
and 'encountering' means nothing other than prayer,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעַד הָעָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: as it says: "And you, do not pray for this people
and do not raise up for them song and prayer
and do not encounter Me"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא supporting רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view that the תפילות were set up by the אבות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 28:11, read together with ירמיהו 7:16 ('encountering' means prayer).

steps.title: The deadline for שחרית follows the morning תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא for רבי יהושע בן לוי: שחרית can be said until חצות because the morning תמיד can be brought until חצות. רבי יהודה says until four hours, because in his view the תמיד can be brought only until four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי says: Why did they say that the morning תפילה can be said until midday? Because the morning תמיד can be brought until midday. רבי יהודה says: until four hours into the day, because the morning תמיד can be brought until four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the second ברייתא, which supports רבי יהושע בן לוי. It shows that the time limit for שחרית is copied from the time limit for the morning תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תפילות were set up to match the קרבנות, their times should match too, and that is exactly what this ברייתא says. Even רבי יהודה, who gives a different deadline, uses the same reasoning. He only disagrees about how late the תמיד itself can be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Midday
The morning תמיד, the daily morning קרבן
Can keep being brought
Four hours into the day

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not arguing against רבי יהושע בן לוי's idea. Both sides of this ברייתא agree that שחרית follows the תמיד. They only argue about the deadline of the תמיד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains where the deadlines in our משנה come from: they come from the times of the קרבנות in the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And it was taught in agreement with רבי יהושע בן לוי:
Why did they say
that the morning prayer may be said until midday?
Because the morning daily offering
may keep being brought until midday.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת
phrases.english: And רבי יהודה says: until four hours,
because the morning daily offering
may keep being brought until four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר עַד חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא to the ברייתא for רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that the תפילות were set up to match the תמידין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that ties the deadline for שחרית to the deadline for the morning תמיד, according to both the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The time for מנחה follows the afternoon daily offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says מנחה may be said until evening because the afternoon תמיד could be brought until evening. רבי יהודה says only until פלג המנחה, because in his view that is the cut-off for the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say מנחה can be prayed until evening? Because the afternoon daily offering could be brought until evening. רבי יהודה says until the midpoint of the afternoon, because the afternoon daily offering could be brought only until then.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its pattern from שחרית and now explains the time for מנחה. It ties the deadline for מנחה to the deadline of the afternoon תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is more support for רבי יהושע בן לוי's idea that תפילות were set up to match the קרבנות. The two opinions argue about how late the afternoon תמיד could be brought, so they also argue about how late you can say מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon prayer
The afternoon; the time for the second daily offering
Can keep being offered (all the way until a certain time)
The midpoint of the afternoon מנחה period

phrases.english: And why did they say
that the afternoon prayer may be said until evening?
Because the afternoon daily offering
phrases.notes: Literally "between the evenings." It is the usual name for the afternoon, when the second תמיד was brought.

phrases.english: could keep being offered until evening.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: only until the midpoint of the afternoon,
because the afternoon daily offering
could be offered only until the midpoint of the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה עַד הָעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Step 11, moving from שחרית to מנחה
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that the תפילות match the קרבנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: the time for מנחה follows the time of the afternoon תמיד

steps.title: Why ערבית has no fixed time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that ערבית has no set time limit because leftover limbs and fats on the מזבח could keep burning all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say the evening prayer has no fixed time? Because limbs and fats that had not finished burning by evening could keep being offered the whole night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains ערבית. Its open-ended time matches the leftover parts of קרבנות that burned on the מזבח through the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was no special evening קרבן, so ערבית is linked to the burning of leftover parts. Since that burning had no fixed end and could last all night, ערבית also has no fixed time.

keyTerms.meaning: The evening prayer (ערבית)
It has no fixed time
Limbs and fats of the קרבנות
Were burned up, finished by the fire

phrases.english: And why did they say
that the evening prayer has no fixed time?
Because limbs and fats
that were not burned up by evening
could keep being offered the whole night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הָעֶרֶב אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from מנחה to ערבית
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that the תפילות match the קרבנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: ערבית matches the burning of leftover limbs and fats through the night

steps.title: The time for מוסף follows the additional offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says מוסף may be said all day because the מוסף קרבן could be brought all day. רבי יהודה says only until seven hours, because that is when the מוסף קרבן could be brought until.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say מוסף can be prayed all day? Because the additional offering could be brought all day. רבי יהודה says until seven hours, because the additional offering could be brought only until seven hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the time for מוסף. Like the others, it matches the time of its קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again רבי יהודה gives an earlier cut-off, because he holds the מוסף קרבן had an earlier deadline. This completes the match between all the תפילות and the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional prayer or offering (on שבת, ראש חודש and יום טוב)
The additional offering
Seven hours into the day

phrases.english: And why did they say
that the additional prayer may be said all day?
Because the additional offering
could be offered all day.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: only until seven hours,
because the additional offering
could be offered only until seven hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ שֶׁל מוּסָפִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from ערבית to מוסף
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that the תפילות match the קרבנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: the time for מוסף follows the time of the מוסף קרבן

steps.title: Defining the early and late times of מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines מנחה גדולה as starting from six and a half hours into the day, and מנחה קטנה as starting from nine and a half hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is the 'big' מנחה? From six and a half hours and on. Which is the 'small' מנחה? From nine and a half hours and on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by explaining two terms: the early מנחה time and the later מנחה time. It gives the starting hour of each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה has two starting points, an early one and a later one. Because there are two periods, it is unclear which one רבי יהודה's פלג המנחה from Step 12 refers to. The next step asks exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'big' (early) מנחה time
The 'small' (later) מנחה time
And a half
And onward, from then on

steps.whatToRemember: Each תפילה's time follows its matching קרבן: מנחה follows the afternoon תמיד, ערבית follows the leftover parts burning at night, and מוסף follows the מוסף קרבן. מנחה גדולה begins at six and a half hours, and מנחה קטנה begins at nine and a half hours.
steps.confusionAlert: The hours here are counted from the start of the day, not by the clock. Six and a half hours means half an hour after midday, not 6:30.

phrases.english: And which is the 'big' afternoon time?
From six and a half hours and on.
phrases.notes: Counted from the start of the day, so this is half an hour after midday.

phrases.english: And which is the 'small' afternoon time?
From nine and a half hours and on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא by defining the two מנחה times connected to Step 12
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that the תפילות match the קרבנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the same ברייתא, defining the מנחה time periods

steps.title: Which midpoint of מנחה does רבי יהודה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's cut-off of פלג המנחה is the midpoint of the early מנחה or of the late מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when רבי יהודה says 'פלג המנחה', does he mean the midpoint of the first מנחה or the midpoint of the last מנחה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the cut-off רבי יהודה gave for מנחה. We just learned there are two מנחה time-periods, so which one's midpoint does he mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 defined two periods: מנחה גדולה starts at six and a half hours and מנחה קטנה starts at nine and a half hours. Each one has a different midpoint, so 'פלג המנחה' is unclear. The question is simply which period רבי יהודה was splitting in half.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the students in the בית מדרש)
The midpoint (literally 'half') of the מנחה period
First / earlier
Last / later

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, פְּלַג מִנְחָה קַמָּא קָאָמַר
phrases.english: Does רבי יהודה mean the midpoint of the first מנחה,
phrases.notes: The 'first מנחה' is מנחה גדולה, which starts at six and a half hours, as in the ברייתא just before.

phrases.english: or does he mean the midpoint of the last מנחה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two מנחה periods defined in step 15 to clarify רבי יהודה's cut-off from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's פלג המנחה is the midpoint of מנחה גדולה or of מנחה קטנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the later מנחה, eleven hours minus a quarter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה directly: he meant the midpoint of the last מנחה, which is eleven hours minus a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, 'They meant the midpoint of the last מנחה, which is eleven hours minus a quarter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה himself explains what he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה קטנה runs from nine and a half hours until the end of the day at twelve hours, so it lasts two and a half hours. Half of that is one and a quarter hours. So its midpoint is ten and three quarters hours, which is 'eleven hours minus a quarter'.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source that answers the question)
As a ברייתא teaches
Minus a quarter (of an hour)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, פלג המנחה is one and a quarter hours before the end of the day, at eleven hours minus a quarter.
steps.confusionAlert: These are 'hours of the day': the daylight is split into twelve equal parts. So 'eleven hours' means eleven of those parts after the day begins, not 11 o'clock.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי יהודה says:
They meant the midpoint of the last מנחה,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר רְבִיעַ.
phrases.english: and that is eleven hours minus a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה means the midpoint of מנחה קטנה: eleven hours minus a quarter.

steps.title: Does this disprove רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא?
steps.stepSummary: Since this ברייתא ties each prayer's time to a קרבן, the גמרא suggests it refutes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said the אבות set up the תפלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, because the ברייתא in steps 11 to 15 bases the prayer times on the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said the אבות set up the תפלות, and in step 6 רבי יהושע בן לוי said the תפלות were set up to match the תמידין. The ברייתא in steps 11 to 14 sets every prayer time by its matching קרבן. That seems to fit only רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say
A refutation (a strong challenge to a view)
The אמורא who holds that the אבות set up the תפלות

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the series of ברייתות in steps 11 to 14 and turns it against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view that the אבות set up the תפלות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the prayer times follow the קרבנות, then the תפלות seem to come from the קרבנות, not from the אבות.

steps.title: The אבות set up the prayers; the רבנן tied them to the קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא can answer: the אבות set up the תפלות, and later the רבנן connected them to the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא could tell you: really, I hold that the אבות set up the תפלות, and the רבנן attached them to the קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. Both ideas can be true together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayers began with the אבות. Later the רבנן based details, such as the time limits, on the קרבנות. So the ברייתא proves only that the rules are linked to the קרבנות. It does not prove where the prayers started.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I will tell you (I keep my original position)
The אבות set them up
And they attached them / based them on

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא could say to you:
Really, I will tell you,
the prayers, the אבות set them up,
and the רבנן based them on the קרבנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combines both views: the prayers come from the אבות, and their rules come from the קרבנות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Linking prayer times to the קרבנות means the תפלות come from the קרבנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תפלות began with the אבות, and the רבנן based their details on the קרבנות.

steps.title: Proof from תפלת מוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the answer: otherwise, who set up תפלת מוסף? So the אבות set up the תפלות, and the רבנן based them on the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say this, then according to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who set up תפלת מוסף? Rather, the אבות set up the תפלות, and the רבנן based them on the קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer by pointing to מוסף. Then it repeats the answer as the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבות set up only שחרית, מנחה and ערבית, and none of them set up מוסף. So מוסף must come from the רבנן, modeled on the קרבן מוסף. That shows that even רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא agrees the רבנן connected the תפלות to the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you don't say so
The additional prayer said on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש
Who set it up?

steps.whatToRemember: Even according to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, the אבות set up the תפלות, and the רבנן tied their rules to the קרבנות. מוסף proves this.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: then according to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, תפלת מוסף,
who set it up?
Rather, the אבות set up the prayers,
and the רבנן based them on the קרבנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 19 and closes this discussion.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא also agrees the רבנן based the תפלות on the קרבנות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The existence of תפלת מוסף, which did not come from the אבות.

steps.title: Does 'until four hours' include the fourth hour?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's 'until four hours' from the משנה and asks whether 'until' includes the fourth hour or stops before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: until four hours. They asked: does 'until' mean up to and including, or up to but not including?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks how to read the word 'until' in רבי יהודה's limit for שחרית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until four hours' could mean you may pray through the end of the fourth hour. It could also mean you must finish before the fourth hour starts. The difference is one full hour of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to and including
Up to but not including
Or perhaps

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: until four hours.
A question was raised before them:
Does it mean up to and including,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל?!
phrases.english: or perhaps up to but not including?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to start a new question about רבי יהודה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's 'until four hours' includes the fourth hour.

steps.title: Trying to prove the answer from 'until פלג המנחה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from רבי יהודה's other ruling, 'until פלג המנחה'. If 'until' does not include, he really disagrees with the רבנן. If it does include, the argument begins to show a problem, and it finishes in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, until פלג המנחה. If you say 'up to but not including', that is why there is a difference between רבי יהודה and the רבנן. But if you say 'up to and including', then רבי יהודה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof. It uses how רבי יהודה uses 'until' in his מנחה ruling to show how he uses it for שחרית. This sentence continues past the end of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רבי יהודה uses the word 'until' the same way in both rulings. Reading it as 'not including' leaves a real difference between him and the רבנן, who say מנחה lasts until evening. The גמרא is about to argue that the 'including' reading creates a problem for that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
That is why there is a difference between
But if you say

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says:
until פלג המנחה.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל —
phrases.english: It works well if you say 'up to but not including':

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: that is why there is a difference between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
phrases.notes: The רבנן say מנחה lasts until evening, as in step 12.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל,
phrases.english: But if you say 'up to and including',
רבי יהודה...

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 21 using רבי יהודה's ruling about מנחה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's 'until' means up to but not including.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling 'until פלג המנחה' in the משנה, compared with the רבנן's 'until evening'.
